1	# Global CO₂ Emissions: Trends, Regional Shifts, and Per Capita Inequalities
     2	
     3	## Source
     4	https://climate.nasa.gov/vital-signs/carbon-dioxide/ and Our World in Data — CO₂ and Greenhouse Gas Emissions (Global Carbon Budget 2025)
     5	
     6	## Atmospheric CO₂ Concentration
     7	
     8	The latest measurement from NOAA's Mauna Loa Observatory (February 2026) records atmospheric CO₂ at **429 parts per million (ppm)**. This represents a more than 50% increase from the pre-industrial baseline of approximately 280 ppm. The current level is at least 1.5 times greater than the natural increase observed at the end of the last ice age 20,000 years ago — a change that took thousands of years then but has occurred in roughly two centuries now. Ground-based and satellite measurements confirm the sharp acceleration, linked primarily to the burning of coal, oil, and natural gas.
     9	
    10	## Global Emissions Trajectory (1750–2024)
    11	
    12	Before the Industrial Revolution, CO₂ emissions were negligible. Growth remained relatively slow until the mid-20th century. In **1950**, the world emitted roughly **6 billion tonnes** of CO₂. By **1990**, emissions had nearly quadrupled to over **20 billion tonnes**. Today, global annual emissions from fossil fuels and industry exceed **35 billion tonnes**. While emissions growth has slowed in recent years, they have not yet peaked.
    13	
    14	![Annual CO₂ emissions by country](./assets/figure_3.jpg)
    15	
    16	## Who Emits the Most? Country-Level Totals
    17	
    18	China is the world's largest emitter by a significant margin, producing over 12 billion tonnes annually — more than one-quarter of the global total. The United States peaked near 6 billion tonnes around 2005 and has since declined to roughly 5 billion tonnes. India has risen rapidly to approximately 3 billion tonnes. Europe's share has fallen substantially.
    19	
    20	| Country / Region | Approx. Annual CO₂ (billion t) | Share of Global | Trend (recent) |
    21	|---|---|---|---|
    22	| China | ~12.5 | ~27% | Slight increase |
    23	| United States | ~5.0 | ~14% | Declining |
    24	| India | ~3.0 | ~8% | Rising |
    25	| EU-27 | ~2.7 | ~7% | Declining |
    26	| Germany | ~0.6 | ~1.7% | Declining |
    27	| United Kingdom | ~0.3 | ~0.9% | Declining |
    28	| Brazil | ~0.5 | ~1.4% | Roughly stable |
    29	| France | ~0.3 | ~0.8% | Declining |
    30	
    31	In 1900, Europe and the US accounted for more than 90% of global emissions. By 1950, they still represented over 85%. Today, they account for less than one-third, while Asia — home to nearly 60% of the world's population — produces roughly half of all emissions. Africa and South America each contribute only 3–4%, comparable to international aviation and shipping combined.
    32	
    33	## Per Capita Emissions: Extreme Inequalities
    34	
    35	Per capita CO₂ emissions reveal stark global inequalities. The world's highest per capita emitters are major oil-producing nations with small populations (Qatar, UAE, Bahrain, Kuwait). Among large, populous countries, the US, Australia, and Canada have per capita emissions roughly three times the global average.
    36	
    37	![Per capita CO₂ emissions over time](./assets/figure_1.jpg)
    38	
    39	| Country | Per Capita CO₂ (tonnes/year) |
    40	|---|---|
    41	| United States | ~15 |
    42	| Canada | ~13 |
    43	| Australia | ~15 |
    44	| South Africa | ~8 |
    45	| China | ~9 |
    46	| EU-27 | ~7 |
    47	| World average | ~5 |
    48	| United Kingdom | ~4 |
    49	| France | ~4 |
    50	| India | ~2 |
    51	| Kenya | <1 |
    52	| Chad / Niger | ~0.1 |
    53	
    54	The gap between the highest and lowest per capita emitters is approximately **150-fold**: the average American or Australian emits in under two days what the average person in Chad or Niger emits in an entire year. Importantly, countries with similar living standards can differ significantly — France and the UK have much lower per capita emissions than Germany or the Netherlands, largely because of their energy mix (higher nuclear and renewable shares).
    55	
    56	## 2024 Annual Change in Emissions
    57	
    58	The 2024 map of annual percentage change in CO₂ emissions shows a mixed picture. The United States and much of Europe recorded declines (roughly −1% to −5%), shown in blue. Russia, parts of Southeast Asia, and several African nations saw increases of +2% to +10% or more, shown in orange and red. Some countries in South America (notably one or two) experienced very large percentage increases (>10%), while others saw declines.
    59	
    60	![Annual percentage change in CO₂ emissions, 2024](./assets/figure_4.jpg)
    61	
    62	## Key Findings
    63	
    64	- **Global CO₂ emissions now exceed 35 billion tonnes per year** and have not yet peaked, despite slowing growth rates.
    65	- **China alone accounts for over 25% of global emissions** (~12.5 Bt), more than double the United States (~5 Bt); India (~3 Bt) is the third-largest and rising fast.
    66	- **The geographic center of emissions has shifted dramatically**: from >90% in Europe and the US in 1900 to Asia producing ~50% today, while the US and Europe combined are below one-third.
    67	- **Per capita inequalities are extreme** — a 150× gap separates the highest emitters (US, Australia at ~15 t/person) from the lowest (Chad, Niger at ~0.1 t/person).
    68	- **Energy mix and policy choices matter**: countries with similar prosperity levels (e.g., France vs. Germany) can have very different per capita emissions depending on their reliance on nuclear, renewables, or fossil fuels.

    52	# PPTX Manipulation Skill
    53	
    54	## Overview
    55	
    56	This skill enables programmatic creation, editing, and manipulation of Microsoft PowerPoint (.pptx) presentations using the **python-pptx** library. Create professional slides with text, shapes, images, charts, and tables without manual editing.
    57	
    58	## How to Use
    59	
    60	1. Describe the presentation you want to create or modify
    61	2. Provide content, data, or images to include
    62	3. I'll generate python-pptx code and execute it
    63	
    64	**Example prompts:**
    65	- "Create a 10-slide pitch deck from this outline"
    66	- "Add a chart to slide 3 with this data"
    67	- "Extract all text from this presentation"
    68	- "Generate slides from this markdown content"
    69	
    70	## Domain Knowledge
    71	
    72	### python-pptx Fundamentals
    73	
    74	```python
    75	from pptx import Presentation
    76	from pptx.util import Inches, Pt
    77	from pptx.enum.shapes import MSO_SHAPE
    78	from pptx.enum.text import PP_ALIGN
    79	
    80	# Create new presentation
    81	prs = Presentation()
    82	
    83	# Or open existing
    84	prs = Presentation('existing.pptx')
    85	```
    86	
    87	### Presentation Structure
    88	```
    89	Presentation
    90	├── slide_layouts (predefined layouts)
    91	├── slides (individual slides)
    92	│   ├── shapes (text, images, charts)
    93	│   │   ├── text_frame (paragraphs)
    94	│   │   └── table (rows, cells)
    95	│   └── placeholders (title, content)
    96	└── slide_masters (templates)
    97	```
    98	
    99	### Slide Layouts
   100	```python
   101	# Common layout indices (may vary by template)
   102	TITLE_SLIDE = 0
   103	TITLE_CONTENT = 1
   104	SECTION_HEADER = 2
   105	TWO_CONTENT = 3
   106	COMPARISON = 4
   107	TITLE_ONLY = 5
   108	BLANK = 6
   109	
   110	# Add slide with layout
   111	slide_layout = prs.slide_layouts[TITLE_CONTENT]
   112	slide = prs.slides.add_slide(slide_layout)
   113	```
   114	
   115	### Adding Content
   116	
   117	#### Title Slide
   118	```python
   119	slide_layout = prs.slide_layouts[0]  # Title slide
   120	slide = prs.slides.add_slide(slide_layout)
   121	
   122	title = slide.shapes.title
   123	subtitle = slide.placeholders[1]
   124	
   125	title.text = "Quarterly Report"
   126	subtitle.text = "Q4 2024 Performance Review"
   127	```
   128	
   129	#### Text Content
   130	```python
   131	# Using placeholder
   132	body = slide.placeholders[1]
   133	tf = body.text_frame
   134	tf.text = "First bullet point"
   135	
   136	# Add more paragraphs
   137	p = tf.add_paragraph()
   138	p.text = "Second bullet point"
   139	p.level = 0
   140	
   141	p = tf.add_paragraph()
   142	p.text = "Sub-bullet"
   143	p.level = 1
   144	```

   146	#### Text Box

   148	from pptx.util import Inches, Pt

   158	p = tf.paragraphs[0]

   163	
   164	#### Shapes
   165	```python
   166	from pptx.enum.shapes import MSO_SHAPE
   167	
   168	# Rectangle
   169	shape = slide.shapes.add_shape(
   170	    MSO_SHAPE.RECTANGLE,

   174	shape.text = "Rectangle with text"

   176	# Common shapes:

   178	# MSO_SHAPE.OVAL, CHEVRON, ARROW_RIGHT

   180	```
   181	
   182	#### Images
   183	```python
   184	# Add image
   185	slide.shapes.add_picture(
   186	    'image.png',
   187	    Inches(1), Inches(2),  # position

   189	)
   190	
   191	# Or specify both dimensions

   198	
   199	### Tables
   200	```python
   201	# Create table
   202	rows, cols = 4, 3
   203	left = Inches(1)
   204	top = Inches(2)
   205	width = Inches(8)
   206	height = Inches(2)
   207	
   208	table = slide.shapes.add_table(rows, cols, left, top, width, height).table
   209	
   210	# Set column widths
   211	table.columns[0].width = Inches(2)
   212	table.columns[1].width = Inches(3)
   213	table.columns[2].width = Inches(3)
   214	
   215	# Add headers
   216	headers = ['Product', 'Q3 Sales', 'Q4 Sales']
   217	for i, header in enumerate(headers):
   218	    cell = table.cell(0, i)
   219	    cell.text = header
   220	    cell.text_frame.paragraphs[0].font.bold = True
   221	
   222	# Add data
   223	data = [
   224	    ['Widget A', '$10,000', '$12,500'],
   225	    ['Widget B', '$8,000', '$9,200'],
   226	    ['Widget C', '$15,000', '$18,000'],
   227	]
   228	for row_idx, row_data in enumerate(data, 1):
   229	    for col_idx, value in enumerate(row_data):
   230	        table.cell(row_idx, col_idx).text = value
   231	```

   233	### Charts
   234	```python
   235	from pptx.chart.data import CategoryChartData
   236	from pptx.enum.chart import XL_CHART_TYPE
   237	
   238	# Chart data
   239	chart_data = CategoryChartData()

   256	### Formatting
   257	
   258	#### Text Formatting
   259	```python

   261

   269	
   270	#### Shape Fill & Line
   271	```python
   272	from pptx.dml.color import RGBColor
   273	
   274	shape.fill.solid()
   275	shape.fill.fore_color.rgb = RGBColor(0x00, 0x80, 0x00)
   276	
   277	shape.line.color.rgb = RGBColor(0x00, 0x00, 0x00)
   278	shape.line.width = Pt(2)

   280	
   281	#### Paragraph Alignment
   282	```python
   283	from pptx.enum.text import PP_ALIGN
   284	
   285	p.alignment = PP_ALIGN.CENTER  # LEFT, RIGHT, JUSTIFY
   286	```
   287	
   288	## Best Practices
   289	
   290	1. **Use Templates**: Start with a .pptx template for consistent branding
   291	2. **Layout First**: Plan slide structure before coding
   292	3. **Reuse Slide Masters**: Maintain consistency across presentations
   293	4. **Optimize Images**: Compress images before adding
   294	5. **Test Output**: Always verify generated presentations
   295	
   296	## Common Patterns
   297	
   298	### Slide Deck Generator
   299	```python
   300	def create_deck(title, slides_content):
   301	    prs = Presentation()
   302	    
   303	    # Title slide
   304	    slide = prs.slides.add_slide(prs.slide_layouts[0])
   305	    slide.shapes.title.text = title
   306	    
   307	    # Content slides
   308	    for slide_data in slides_content:
   309	        slide = prs.slides.add_slide(prs.slide_layouts[1])
   310	        slide.shapes.title.text = slide_data['title']
   311	        
   312	        body = slide.placeholders[1]
   313	        tf = body.text_frame
   314	        for i, point in enumerate(slide_data['points']):
   315	            if i == 0:
   316	                tf.text = point
   317	            else:
   318	                p = tf.add_paragraph()
   319	                p.text = point
   320	    
   321	    return prs
   322	```
   323	
   324	### Data-Driven Charts
   325	```python
   326	def add_bar_chart(slide, title, categories, values):
   327	    from pptx.chart.data import CategoryChartData
   328	    from pptx.enum.chart import XL_CHART_TYPE
   329	    
   330	    chart_data = CategoryChartData()
   331	    chart_data.categories = categories
   332	    chart_data.add_series('Values', values)
   333	    
   334	    chart = slide.shapes.add_chart(
   335	        XL_CHART_TYPE.BAR_CLUSTERED,
   336	        Inches(1), Inches(2),
   337	        Inches(8), Inches(4),
   338	        chart_data
   339	    ).chart
   340	    
   341	    chart.chart_title.text_frame.text = title
   342	    return chart
   343	```

   345	## Examples
   346	
   347	### Example 1: Create a Pitch Deck
   348	```python
   349	from pptx import Presentation

   351	
   352	prs = Presentation()

   356	slide.shapes.title.text = "StartupX"

   359	# Slide 2: Problem

   368	# Slide 3: Solution

   370	slide.shapes.title.text = "Our Solution"
   371	body = slide.placeholders[1].text_frame

   373	body.add_paragraph().text = "90% faster processing"
   374	body.add_paragraph().text = "99.5% accuracy"

   377	# Slide 4: Market
   378	slide = prs.slides.add_slide(prs.slide_layouts[5])  # Title only
   379	slide.shapes.title.text = "Market Opportunity: $50B by 2028"
   380

   382	from pptx.chart.data import CategoryChartData
   383	from pptx.enum.chart import XL_CHART_TYPE
   384	
   385	data = CategoryChartData()

   387	data.add_series('Market Size ($B)', [30, 35, 40, 45, 50])
   388	
   389	slide.shapes.add_chart(
   390	    XL_CHART_TYPE.LINE,
   391	    Inches(1), Inches(1.5),
   392	    Inches(8), Inches(5),

   396	prs.save('pitch_deck.pptx')

   399	### Example 2: Report with Data Table
   400	```python
   401	from pptx import Presentation
   402	from pptx.util import Inches, Pt
   403	
   404	prs = Presentation()
   405	
   406	# Title slide
   407	slide = prs.slides.add_slide(prs.slide_layouts[0])
   408	slide.shapes.title.text = "Sales Performance Report"
   409	slide.placeholders[1].text = "Q4 2024"

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
Build a 9-slide, 16:9 PowerPoint presentation on Global CO₂ Emissions.
Data-forward, analytical, authoritative tone for policy analysts and climate negotiators.
"""

from pptx import Presentation
from pptx.util import Inches, Pt, Emu
from pptx.enum.text import PP_ALIGN, MSO_ANCHOR
from pptx.enum.shapes import MSO_SHAPE
from pptx.dml.color import RGBColor
from pptx.enum.chart import XL_CHART_TYPE, XL_LEGEND_POSITION
from pptx.chart.data import CategoryChartData
import os

# ── Constants ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
ASSETS_DIR = "/app/benchmark/assets"
OUTPUT_PATH = "/app/output/final_deck.pptx"

# Color palette: dark, authoritative, data-forward
DARK_BG = RGBColor(0x1A, 0x1A, 0x1A)       # near-black for title slide
DARK_TEXT = RGBColor(0x1A, 0x1A, 0x1A)     # body text
LIGHT_TEXT = RGBColor(0xF5, 0xF5, 0xF5)    # light text on dark bg
ACCENT_TEAL = RGBColor(0x00, 0x8C, 0x8C)   # accent
ACCENT_ORANGE = RGBColor(0xE6, 0x5C, 0x00) # highlight
ACCENT_BLUE = RGBColor(0x2E, 0x5E, 0xAA)   # chart blue
ACCENT_GREEN = RGBColor(0x2E, 0x7D, 0x32)  # chart green
ACCENT_RED = RGBColor(0xC6, 0x28, 0x28)    # chart red
ACCENT_GRAY = RGBColor(0x75, 0x75, 0x75)   # muted
WHITE = RGBColor(0xFF, 0xFF, 0xFF)
SLIGHT_GRAY = RGBColor(0xF7, 0xF7, 0xF7)

# ── Helpers ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
def set_slide_bg(slide, color):
    """Set solid background color for a slide."""
    background = slide.background
    fill = background.fill
    fill.solid()
    fill.fore_color.rgb = color

def add_text_box(slide, left, top, width, height, text, font_size=Pt(14),
                 font_color=DARK_TEXT, bold=False, italic=False,
                 align=PP_ALIGN.LEFT, font_name="Calibri"):
    """Add a text box with formatting."""
    txBox = slide.shapes.add_textbox(left, top, width, height)
    tf = txBox.text_frame
    tf.word_wrap = True
    p = tf.paragraphs[0]
    p.text = text
    p.font.size = font_size
    p.font.color.rgb = font_color
    p.font.bold = bold
    p.font.italic = italic
    p.font.name = font_name
    p.alignment = align
    return txBox

def add_bullet_text(slide, left, top, width, height, bullets,
                    font_size=Pt(16), font_color=DARK_TEXT, font_name="Calibri",
                    bullet_color=ACCENT_TEAL):
    """Add a text box with bullet paragraphs."""
    txBox = slide.shapes.add_textbox(left, top, width, height)
    tf = txBox.text_frame
    tf.word_wrap = True
    for i, bullet in enumerate(bullets):
        if i == 0:
            p = tf.paragraphs[0]
        else:
            p = tf.add_paragraph()
        p.text = bullet
        p.font.size = font_size
        p.font.color.rgb = font_color
        p.font.name = font_name
        p.level = 0
        p.space_after = Pt(10)
    return txBox

def style_title(title_shape, text):
    """Style a title shape."""
    title_shape.text = text
    tf = title_shape.text_frame
    p = tf.paragraphs[0]
    p.font.size = Pt(32)
    p.font.bold = True
    p.font.color.rgb = DARK_TEXT
    p.font.name = "Calibri"
    p.alignment = PP_ALIGN.LEFT

def style_subtitle(subtitle_shape, text):
    """Style a subtitle shape."""
    subtitle_shape.text = text
    tf = subtitle_shape.text_frame
    p = tf.paragraphs[0]
    p.font.size = Pt(16)
    p.font.color.rgb = ACCENT_GRAY
    p.font.name = "Calibri"
    p.alignment = PP_ALIGN.LEFT

# ── Build Presentation ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────
prs = Presentation()
prs.slide_width = Inches(13.333)
prs.slide_height = Inches(7.5)

# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# SLIDE 1 — Title Slide
# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
slide_layout = prs.slide_layouts[6]  # Blank
slide1 = prs.slides.add_slide(slide_layout)
set_slide_bg(slide1, DARK_BG)

# Title
add_text_box(slide1, Inches(0.8), Inches(2.2), Inches(11.5), Inches(1.5),
             "Global CO₂ Emissions: Trends, Regional Shifts, and Per Capita Inequalities",
             font_size=Pt(40), font_color=LIGHT_TEXT, bold=True, align=PP_ALIGN.LEFT)

# Subtitle
add_text_box(slide1, Inches(0.8), Inches(3.6), Inches(11.5), Inches(0.6),
             "A data-driven overview from the Industrial Revolution to 2024",
             font_size=Pt(20), font_color=ACCENT_TEAL, align=PP_ALIGN.LEFT)

# Scope line
add_text_box(slide1, Inches(0.8), Inches(4.3), Inches(11.5), Inches(0.5),
             "Scope: 1750 – 2024  |  Sources: Global Carbon Budget 2025, NASA NOAA Mauna Loa Observatory",
             font_size=Pt(14), font_color=RGBColor(0xAA, 0xAA, 0xAA), align=PP_ALIGN.LEFT)

# Accent bar
bar = slide1.shapes.add_shape(MSO_SHAPE.RECTANGLE, Inches(0.8), Inches(4.9), Inches(2.5), Inches(0.05))
bar.fill.solid()
bar.fill.fore_color.rgb = ACCENT_TEAL
bar.line.fill.background()

# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# SLIDE 2 — Atmospheric CO₂ Milestone
# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
slide2 = prs.slides.add_slide(prs.slide_layouts[6])
set_slide_bg(slide2, WHITE)

# Title bar background
bar2 = slide2.shapes.add_shape(MSO_SHAPE.RECTANGLE, Inches(0), Inches(0), Inches(13.333), Inches(1.1))
bar2.fill.solid()
bar2.fill.fore_color.rgb = SLIGHT_GRAY
bar2.line.fill.background()

add_text_box(slide2, Inches(0.6), Inches(0.25), Inches(12), Inches(0.7),
             "Atmospheric CO₂ Reaches 429 ppm — 50% Above Pre-Industrial Levels",
             font_size=Pt(28), font_color=DARK_TEXT, bold=True, align=PP_ALIGN.LEFT)

# Big stat callout box
box_left, box_top, box_w, box_h = Inches(0.6), Inches(1.6), Inches(5.5), Inches(2.2)
box = slide2.shapes.add_shape(MSO_SHAPE.ROUNDED_RECTANGLE, box_left, box_top, box_w, box_h)
box.fill.solid()
box.fill.fore_color.rgb = RGBColor(0xE8, 0xF4, 0xF4)
box.line.color.rgb = ACCENT_TEAL
box.line.width = Pt(2)

add_text_box(slide2, box_left + Inches(0.3), box_top + Inches(0.3), box_w - Inches(0.6), Inches(0.8),
             "429 ppm", font_size=Pt(48), font_color=ACCENT_TEAL, bold=True, align=PP_ALIGN.LEFT)
add_text_box(slide2, box_left + Inches(0.3), box_top + Inches(1.2), box_w - Inches(0.6), Inches(0.8),
             "Latest measurement from NOAA Mauna Loa Observatory (February 2026)",
             font_size=Pt(14), font_color=DARK_TEXT, align=PP_ALIGN.LEFT)

# Context bullets
bullets2 = [
    "• Pre-industrial baseline: ~280 ppm",
    "• Current level is >1.5× the natural increase observed at the end of the last ice age (20,000 years ago)",
    "• That ancient change took thousands of years; the modern rise has occurred in roughly two centuries",
    "• Ground-based and satellite measurements confirm sharp acceleration, linked primarily to burning coal, oil, and natural gas"
]
add_bullet_text(slide2, Inches(0.6), Inches(4.1), Inches(12), Inches(2.8), bullets2, font_size=Pt(16))

# Timeline annotation (simple visual)
timeline_y = Inches(6.5)
add_text_box(slide2, Inches(0.6), timeline_y, Inches(12), Inches(0.5),
             "Timeline:  280 ppm (pre-industrial)  →  315 ppm (1958)  →  429 ppm (2026)",
             font_size=Pt(14), font_color=ACCENT_GRAY, align=PP_ALIGN.LEFT)
line = slide2.shapes.add_shape(MSO_SHAPE.RECTANGLE, Inches(0.6), timeline_y + Inches(0.35), Inches(11.5), Inches(0.03))
line.fill.solid()
line.fill.fore_color.rgb = ACCENT_TEAL
line.line.fill.background()

# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
# SLIDE 3 — Global Emissions Trajectory
# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
slide3 = prs.slides.add_slide(prs.slide_layouts[6])
set_slide_bg(slide3, WHITE)

bar3 = slide3.shapes.add_shape(MSO_SHAPE.RECTANGLE, Inches(0), Inches(0), Inches(13.333), Inches(1.1))
bar3.fill.solid()
bar3.fill.fore_color.rgb = SLIGHT_GRAY
bar3.line.fill.background()

add_text_box(slide3, Inches(0.6), Inches(0.25), Inches(12), Inches(0.7),
             "Global Fossil Fuel CO₂ Emissions Grew Six-Fold: 6 Billion to 35+ Billion Tonnes",
             font_size=Pt(28), font_color=DARK_TEXT, bold=True, align=PP_ALIGN.LEFT)

# Chart data
chart_data3 = CategoryChartData()
chart_data3.categories = ['1750', '1850', '1900', '1950', '1970', '1990', '2010', '2024']
chart_data3.add_series('Global CO₂ Emissions (billion tonnes)', (0.0, 0.2, 1.9, 6.0, 14.0, 22.0, 33.0, 37.0))

x, y, cx, cy = Inches(0.6), Inches(1.5), Inches(7.5), Inches(4.5)
chart3 = slide3.shapes.add_chart(XL_CHART_TYPE.LINE_MARKED, x, y, cx, cy, chart_data3).chart
chart3.has_legend = True
chart3.legend.position = XL_LEGEND_POSITION.BOTTOM
chart3.chart_title.text_frame.text = "Global CO₂ Emissions from Fossil Fuels & Industry"

# Key inflection callouts on right
inflections = [
    ("1950", "~6 billion tonnes", "Post-war industrial acceleration begins"),
    ("1990", "~22 billion tonnes", "Nearly quadrupled since 1950"),
    ("2024", ">35 billion tonnes", "Growth slowed but not yet peaked"),

box_x = Inches(8.5)
for i, (year, val, desc) in enumerate(inflections):
    y_pos = Inches(1.6) + i * Inches(1.5)
    # rounded rect
    r = slide3.shapes.add_shape(MSO_SHAPE.ROUNDED_RECTANGLE, box_x, y_pos, Inches(4.0), Inches(1.2))
    r.fill.solid()
    r.fill.fore_color.rgb = SLIGHT_GRAY

    r.line.width = Pt(1)
    add_text_box(slide3, box_x + Inches(0.15), y_pos + Inches(0.1), Inches(3.7), Inches(0.4),
                 f"{year}: {val}", font_size=Pt(16), font_color=DARK_TEXT, bold=True)
    add_text_box(slide3, box_x + Inches(0.15), y_pos + Inches(0.5), Inches(3.7), Inches(0.6),
                 desc, font_size=Pt(13), font_color=ACCENT_GRAY)

# Figure reference
add_text_box(slide3, Inches(0.6), Inches(6.2), Inches(12), Inches(0.4),
             "Reference: figure_2.jpg — Annual CO₂ emissions trajectory (Global Carbon Budget 2025)",
             font_size=Pt(12), font_color=ACCENT_GRAY, italic=True)

# ═══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════

slide4 = prs.slides.add_slide(prs.slide_layouts[6])

bar4 = slide4.shapes.add_shape(MSO_SHAPE.RECTANGLE, Inches(0), Inches(0), Inches(13.333), Inches(1.1))
bar4.fill.solid()

bar4.line.fill.background()

add_text_box(slide4, Inches(0.6), Inches(0.25), Inches(12), Inches(0.7),

# Data table
rows, cols = 9, 4
left = Inches(0.6)
top = Inches(1.5)

table4.columns[0].width = Inches(2.5)
table4.columns[1].width = Inches(2.5)

for i, h in enumerate(headers):

data4 = [

# Right-side insight box
